Messages.Author: joseph mcevoy
Messages.Body:
Ok, here's a wierd one.

My predator comes in to bleed me with a minion, which I block with
one of my minions. He plays 'Form of Mist', and since he has superior the
action continues at plus one stealth.

Can I play a 'Fast Reaction' card and enter combat again (with
another minion, of course)? Common sense would say yes.

BUT- once that round of combat is over, does my predator's minion
get to continue his action at the plus one stealth?

What happens if I put that minion into torpor during the resulting
combat? I would assume that the action is aborted (as if it were blocked).

Just wanted to check, since my predator's "Strike, combat ends, pay
one pool to untap" deck is starting to REALLY annoy me.. and this seems to
be the only way I could conceivably fight back.

Joseph < mcev...@matrix.newpaltz.edu >

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
mcev...@matrix.newpaltz.edu (joseph mcevoy) writes:

> My predator comes in to bleed me with a minion, which I block with
>one of my minions. He plays 'Form of Mist', and since he has superior the
>action continues at plus one stealth.

> Can I play a 'Fast Reaction' card and enter combat again (with
>another minion, of course)? Common sense would say yes.

Yes.

> BUT- once that round of combat is over, does my predator's minion
>get to continue his action at the plus one stealth?

No. DTR 5/9/95:

> 6) "What happens if I play superior Form of Mist to end combat,
> but the blocking minion plays Psyche?"
> Psyche forces a new combat, and the effects of Form of Mist
> are lost.

Fast Reaction falls under this same ruling, IMHO.

> What happens if I put that minion into torpor during the resulting
>combat? I would assume that the action is aborted (as if it were blocked).

Moot.
